intervals.label: operating
intervals.note: Fermilab announced the first observed neutrino interactions on 2024-09-10.
intervals.quote: SBND began operation in July 2024, and started collecting stable neutrino beam data in December 2024 with an unprecedented rate of ~7,000 neutrino events per day.

name: SBND detector
notes: Placed at site:fermilab-main-campus (owned by the fermilab-dune lead): no separately sourceable site record exists for this detector hall in this wave.
The SBN proposal (2015) describes the same detector under its earlier name LAr1-ND, with an active volume of 4.0 x 4.0 x 5.0 m containing 112 tons of liquid argon.
Event rate is not recorded as a quantity: the SBND detector paper states "~7,000 neutrino events per day", and the schema's rate dimension has no per-day unit.

placements.note: Placed at site:fermilab-main-campus (owned by the fermilab-dune lead): no separately sourceable site record exists for this detector hall in this wave. SBND sits in a dedicated building 110 m from the BNB target.

active_mass.quote: SBND is a 112 ton liquid argon time projection chamber (LArTPC) neutrino detector located 110 meters from the Booster Neutrino Beam (BNB) target at Fermilab.

baseline.quote: located 110 meters from the Booster Neutrino Beam (BNB) target at Fermilab

target_medium.quote: 112 ton liquid argon time projection chamber (LArTPC)

summary.plain: A 112-tonne liquid argon camera only 110 metres from where Fermilab makes its Booster neutrino beam. Being so close, it sees about 7,000 neutrinos a day, more than any similar detector.
summary.technical: 112 t active mass single-phase liquid argon TPC 110 m from the Booster Neutrino Beam target, the near detector of the Short-Baseline Neutrino programme; 4.0 x 4.0 x 5.0 m active volume in the SBN proposal design.
